title: What Is the Ideal Humidity for a Crawl Space?
h1: What Is the Ideal Humidity for a Crawl Space?
description: Keep crawl space humidity below about 60 percent, ideally in the 40s to low 50s. Learn the signs of moisture problems and how to dry out a damp crawl space.
quick_answer: Most crawl spaces should stay below about 60 percent relative humidity, and the 40s to low 50s is a better target. Above 60 percent, mold, mildew and wood rot become more likely, and pests are drawn to the dampness. A simple hygrometer placed in the crawl space will tell you where you stand.
body:
A lot of Southern California homes are built on slabs, but plenty of older homes, hillside homes and raised-foundation houses have crawl spaces. They're easy to forget about because nobody goes down there. But the air in a crawl space rises into your home, and whatever is growing down there can affect how your house smells and how you feel.

Why does crawl space humidity matter?

When humidity stays high, problems build up slowly:

  • Mold and mildew grow on wood framing, subfloors and stored items.
  • Wood rot weakens joists and subflooring over time.
  • Pests like termites, ants and rodents are drawn to damp spaces.
  • Insulation under the floor sags and loses its value when it gets wet.
  • Musty odors drift up into living spaces through gaps in the floor.

If you have ducts running through the crawl space, leaks can pull that damp air straight into the system and blow it into every room.

What causes high humidity in a crawl space?

In coastal areas, damp marine air is the main culprit. Other common causes include:

  • Bare soil with no vapor barrier, which releases moisture constantly
  • Poor drainage, downspouts or sprinklers that dump water near the foundation
  • Plumbing leaks under the house
  • Blocked or missing foundation vents
  • Condensation on uninsulated ducts or water lines
  • A dryer vent or bathroom fan that exhausts into the crawl space instead of outside

How do you check crawl space humidity?

Put a digital hygrometer in the crawl space, ideally one with a remote display or one that records highs and lows. Check it over a few weeks and through different weather. Readings above 60 percent are a sign to act.

While you're there, use a flashlight to look for these warning signs:

  • Standing water or wet soil
  • White, green or black growth on wood
  • Water stains or droplets on pipes and ducts
  • Sagging or fallen insulation
  • Rodent droppings or nesting material

Wear a mask and gloves, and don't go in if you see signs of a large rodent infestation. That needs professional cleanup.

How do you lower crawl space humidity?

Start with the water sources, then deal with the air.

  1. Fix drainage. Extend downspouts, regrade soil so it slopes away from the house and adjust sprinklers.
  2. Repair leaks. Any dripping pipe or drain line should be fixed first.
  3. Add a vapor barrier. A heavy plastic sheet over the soil blocks a lot of ground moisture.
  4. Keep vents clear. In many Southern California homes, foundation vents help the space dry out. Make sure plants and debris aren't blocking them.
  5. Seal and insulate ducts. This stops condensation and keeps crawl space air out of your HVAC system.
  6. Consider a dehumidifier. For crawl spaces that stay damp, a dehumidifier designed for that space can hold humidity in a safe range.

Should a crawl space be vented or sealed?

Both approaches can work. A vented crawl space relies on outside air to carry moisture away, which works well in drier inland areas. A sealed, or encapsulated, crawl space closes off vents, lines the walls and floor and controls humidity with a dehumidifier or conditioned air. Encapsulation can make sense in damp coastal locations, but it needs to be designed carefully, especially with gas appliances nearby, and may need to meet local code.

Can high crawl space humidity affect your HVAC system?

It can. In raised-foundation homes, ducts and sometimes the furnace itself run through the crawl space. Leaky return ducts pull crawl space air directly into the system. Damp conditions can also corrode metal duct, loosen duct tape and make insulation on ducts sag or fall off. Uninsulated supply ducts carrying cold AC air can sweat on humid days, dripping water onto the soil and making the problem worse.

When should you call a professional?

If you find mold, rodent activity, wet insulation or damaged ducts, it's time to get help. Our attic, crawl space and insulation team handles cleanup, insulation replacement, vapor barriers and air sealing, and we can check the ductwork while we're there.
faqs: Is 70 percent humidity too high for a crawl space?
Yes. At 70 percent and above, mold and wood rot become much more likely. If readings stay that high, look for drainage problems, leaks or bare soil, and consider a vapor barrier or dehumidifier.
Should I close my crawl space vents in winter?
In most of Southern California, foundation vents are usually left open year-round to help the space dry out. Closing them without a full sealing and humidity control plan can trap moisture.
Can a damp crawl space affect the air in my house?
It can. Air moves upward through gaps in the floor and through leaky ducts. If the crawl space is musty or moldy, those odors and particles can end up in your living spaces.
How often should I check my crawl space?
A quick look once or twice a year is a good habit, and after heavy rain. A hygrometer you can read without going under the house makes it easy to keep tabs on humidity.
